name: Manila
tagline: A sprawling, energetic capital with a walled Spanish citadel, Chinatown food crawls, jeepney chaos and Manila Bay sunsets.
highlight: Walking the ramparts of Fort Santiago in Intramuros as the light softens over the old walled city.
shortDescription: The Philippine capital, with the walled city of Intramuros, San Agustin Church, Binondo Chinatown, Rizal Park, museums, malls and nightlife, and the gateway to the country.
metaDescription: A Manila travel guide: Intramuros, Fort Santiago, San Agustin Church, Binondo Chinatown food crawl, Rizal Park, Manila Bay sunset, museums, safety, where to stay and a two-day plan.

image.alt: Old buildings and streets inside the walled city of Intramuros in Manila

intro: Manila is the capital of the Philippines and the heart of Metro Manila, a huge urban area of about 14 million people made up of 16 cities. It is loud, hot, congested and endlessly busy, and most visitors treat it as a gateway. But with a little planning, it offers real rewards: colonial history, superb food, museums and an infectious energy.

The city was founded by the Spanish in 1571, and Intramuros, the walled city, was the centre of Spanish power in Asia. Its walls, gates, churches and Fort Santiago survive, although much was destroyed in the Second World War, including much of the rest of the old city. San Agustin Church, completed in 1607, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the oldest stone church in the country. Rizal Park, nearby, honours the national hero José Rizal, who was executed in 1896.

Elsewhere, Binondo is the world's oldest Chinatown, and a great place for a food crawl, and Manila Bay is famed for its sunsets. Modern Makati and Bonifacio Global City have malls, restaurants and nightlife. Manila has traffic and pollution, and street crime can occur, so travel with care and use Grab. Two days covers the highlights.
